newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia U-Wood to buy eight companies.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia U-Wood to buy eight companies.

text.p: Malaysia's U-Wood Holdings Bhd said on Wednesday it has proposed to acquire seven property development companies and a project management firm for a total 305.86 million ringgit.
The company also planned a one-for-two rights issue of 16 million new shares at an issue price of 7.0 ringgit a share, U-Wood said in a statement.

Six of the companies to be acquired are developing 600 acres of land in central Selangor state into a mixed residential and commercial development project. U-Wood said the project is expected to be completed by 2005 with total revenue estimated at 1.16 billion ringgit.
U-Wood is also acquiring the company managing the project.

The other company U-Wood is buying is developing 338 acres of land in Selangor into a residential and commercial development. The project, expected to be completed in 2003, is estimated to generate total revenue of 332.3 million ringgit.
The acquisitions will be paid for by cash of 109.86 million ringgit and an issue of 19.6 million new U-Wood shares at 10.0 ringgit each.

U-Wood, which makes and trades plywood, blockboard and timber products, said proceeds of the rights issue would be used as part payment of the acquisitions, to repay borrowings and for working capital.

To accommodate the increase in the company's paid-up capital to 67.6 million ringgit from 32.0 million after the acquisitions and rights issue, U-Wood has proposed to increase its authorised share capital to 100 million ringgit from 50 million.
Shares of U-Wood, suspended since October 23, were last traded at 11.50 ringgit.
